defaults.permitted_development: Detached outbuildings such as sheds, workshops and garden stores can usually be permitted development in England where they are for a purpose incidental to the enjoyment of the house, stay behind the principal elevation, remain single storey and comply with the Class E height and coverage limits. The route does not cover separate self-contained living accommodation.

rules.height_rules: Keep the building single storey with eaves no higher than 2.5m. The overall height limit is 4m for a dual-pitched roof, 3m for any other roof and 2.5m overall if any part sits within 2m of a boundary.
rules.depth_rules: There is no standalone depth allowance. The key tests are whether the building stays within the curtilage, remains behind the principal elevation and keeps the total area covered by additions and outbuildings within 50% of the land around the original house.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary siting matters because any part within 2m of a boundary is capped at 2.5m overall. On designated land, outbuildings at the side of the house can need permission, and any outbuilding in the curtilage of a listed building needs planning permission.
rules.roof_rules: Roof form directly controls the allowed height. A dual-pitched roof can go to 4m, other roofs to 3m, but any part within 2m of a boundary must stay at or below 2.5m overall. Verandas, balconies and raised platforms above 300mm are outside the normal Class E route.
rules.materials_rules: Materials do not have to match exactly, but the building should still read as subordinate and domestic in character. The layout, services and fittings should stay incidental so the structure does not drift into self-contained accommodation.

rules.permitted_development: The ordinary planning route for an outbuilding is usually available where the building is genuinely incidental, single storey and not placed forward of the principal elevation. Separate living use falls outside that fallback. That fallback can disappear where an Article 4 direction or an old planning condition has removed the normal householder right.

rules.height_rules: Height is often the decisive outbuilding test because it determines whether the detached building still reads as modest and subordinate.
rules.depth_rules: The building should stay within the residential curtilage and behind the principal elevation. Combined additions and outbuildings should not cover more than 50% of the land around the original house.
rules.boundary_rules: Within 2 metres of a boundary, the overall height limit drops to 2.5 metres. Boundary-hugging buildings are more likely to raise dominance and neighbour-impact issues.
rules.roof_rules: A bulky or badly positioned roof can cause an outbuilding to exceed the normal Class E limits or lose its subordinate character.
rules.materials_rules: Materials do not need to copy the house exactly, but the building should still read as a subordinate domestic outbuilding.
